agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models the office assistant as a tool-using agent whose model directs goal pursuit and action selection; the scripted worst-case models used in tests still direct the tool call sequence.

evidence.rationale: The entry point is attacker-controlled natural language delivered by injection or a confused request that leads the model to call write_file with a hostile path; the writeup names injection as the source.
evidence_refs: A request leads the model to call write_file with a path such as ../pwned.txt or .env.
Some input makes the model issue the path. The lab names injection or a confused request.

evidence.rationale: The agent has long-term cross-session memory notes presented as trusted instructions in the next session's prompt, so attacker-influenced context persists across sessions.
evidence_refs: A JSON file of free-text notes. In the baseline it is unsigned and never expires, and the next session's system prompt presents the notes as trusted instructions to follow.

evidence.rationale: A single agent with one identity relays the model's decision to its own write_file tool under the same principal and policy domain; the lab states multi-agent setups are out of scope.
evidence_refs: The agent acts with one identity. There is no per-user identity or authorization on tools.

evidence.rationale: The packet contains no evidence about evaluators, verifiers, or reward channels on this path, and no verified or refuted reward-hacking episodes.
Tool arguments are not validated in the baseline and all twelve built-in tools are offered to every task; the assessed write_file path argument is unconstrained.
evidence_refs: Twelve built-in tools are all offered to every task unless a caller passes allowed_tools. Arguments are not validated in the baseline.

scores.basis: Lookup Table AIVSS (Table 6): A0 or AX keep CVSS-BTE unchanged; A1 or A2 take the higher of the band cell and CVSS-BTE. AIVSS is never lower than CVSS-BTE.

title: Over-permissioned write_file: writes outside the workspace and over .env
summary: Arbitrary file creation or modification outside the workspace, including overwriting the workspace credential file.
